summary:
BudgetTracker has been the main project for the past few weeks. The biggest structural change was pulling the database off a shared SQL Server instance and migrating the whole app to Postgres on Supabase — a full Drizzle ORM rewrite with no compatibility shim, since the app was single-user and that was the right window to make breaking changes. 8,239 transactions and 773 merchants landed intact. On top of that, the AI assistant went from a single global model pointed at a local GPU to a proper provider abstraction: users can bring their own Anthropic, OpenAI, or Gemini key, and every query the assistant makes is scoped through the same account-isolation logic the rest of the app uses.

The more recent work has been an MCP server — an in-process Express route that exposes 13 read-only tools (burn rate, spending anomalies, cash flow projection, upcoming obligations, and more) behind scoped, hashed API tokens. The point is that my local AI agent can call `get_daily_briefing` each morning and hand the computed numbers to a local model to phrase a spending summary, without the figures ever leaving the LAN. Wiring that up uncovered a pair of latent Postgres bugs dormant since the database migration: one was a `date - unknown` type error in date arithmetic (fixed with a `::int` cast), and the other was calling `.toISOString()` on a raw-SQL join row where the driver returns strings, not Date objects.

There was also a security audit. Found a path traversal on the receipt-image endpoint that allowed authenticated arbitrary file reads — the `..%2f` sequence escaped the upload directory. Added JWT `type` claims to prevent refresh tokens from being used as Bearer access tokens, wired magic-byte verification before passing uploads to the image processor, and put a SSRF guard on user-supplied LLM base URLs. The guard draws the line at operator-vs-user: the server's own locally-configured model is exempt (so a LAN endpoint keeps working), while any URL a user types must be public HTTPS.

On the feature side, I built income pattern detection for the recurring view. The tricky part was that a 98-deposit clean-biweekly paycheck history was being misidentified as semimonthly — a gap-based cluster count collapsed the whole series to two day-of-month buckets because the deposits were dense. Fixed by switching to distinct monthly bucket counts and restricting detection to the last 12 deposits, so the pattern reflects the current job rather than years of history with gaps. Subscriptions also got a rework: confirming a detected pattern now auto-creates a subscription entry, next-billing dates roll forward on read rather than staying frozen at creation, and merchant deduplication got stronger normalization so `MIDJOURNEY INC` and `Midjourney` stop splitting into two records.

I've also been building a speed-reader that mirrors Claude Code replies and flashes them one word or phrase at a time. Pacing uses a small Haiku call that scores phrase density across a response and returns timing overlays — it influences dwell time only, never rewrites the text. The web version does the credentialed scoring on the server side so the auth token stays out of the browser, and there's a session picker so it follows the right project when multiple Claude sessions are open.

highlights.oneLiner: Income pattern detection live, subscription dedup shipped, security audit complete, MCP toolset at 13 tools
Brain flipped to qwen3.6:35b, toolset trimmed 32K→20K tokens, spending briefing section wired via BT MCP
Dashboard Claude tile cron running; PWA briefing-replay site scoped and in design
Cadence RSVP speed-reader built: TUI + web GUI with server-side Haiku pacing and session picker
